title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
event_hint: Research paper presents KAP (Knowledge Access Planning), a paradigm-shifting execution abstraction for LLM serving that bridges the gap between structured knowledge priors and runtime KV consumption
problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: modern LLM systems produce high-value structured priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, confidence signals) but LLM serving backends observe only flat token sequences after prompt serialization, forcing dense and uniform consumption of full KV state during decoding. This increases latency and degrades throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of context
mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors from passive prompt-construction hints into first-class physical execution artifacts through a universal intermediate representation - the runtime access plan - which compiles structured knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training procedures. Instantiated as GraphSpec compiler-executor connecting Graph-RAG knowledge selection to vLLM serving backend, shifting LLM serving from token-aware context consumption to plan-driven, knowledge-aware runtime consumption

evidence.claim: GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K context length
evidence.condition: 128K context length, long-context QA workload on SPIQA dataset

evidence.claim: GraphSpec achieves 1.08x-1.19x decode throughput speedup over full-context baseline across 4K-128K context lengths
evidence.baseline: Full-context decoding with standard vLLM backend
evidence.condition: SPIQA dataset, 4K-128K context lengths, decode throughput (TPS) measurement

evidence.claim: GraphSpec Top-3 tolerant acceptance rate remains high (0.953-0.962) across all context lengths, indicating proposal effectiveness
evidence.condition: 4K-128K context lengths, Top-3 tolerant proposal acceptance rate metric

evidence.claim: GraphSpec maintains answer quality comparable to full-context decoding, with pass rates differing by at most 1.9 percentage points at 64K (87.9% vs 86.0%)
evidence.condition: 64K context length, LLM similarity pass rate with 0.5 threshold

evidence.claim: Physical concat (prompt materialization without runtime access plan) achieves only 73.9% pass rate vs GraphSpec 87.9% at 64K, proving runtime access plan is essential
evidence.condition: 64K context length, same evidence selected but materialized as shortened prompt

evaluation_context: Evaluated on SPIQA dataset with 4K-128K context lengths using vLLM serving backend. Graph-RAG evidence and priors frozen before benchmarking; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT measurements. LLM-as-judge quality metric with 0.5 threshold independently validated (95% judge-human agreement on 100 sampled answers). Throughput covers complete executor path, not isolated model-forward performance
limitations: Evaluation validates KAP through GraphSpec, a single concrete instantiation with Graph-RAG frontend and vLLM backend. Results strongest for long-context QA workloads where graph-derived priors can be grounded in evidence spans. Effectiveness depends on quality of knowledge priors, compiler's ability to translate into useful runtime access plans, and backend's ability to execute plans without excessive metadata/synchronization overhead. Other KAP instantiations may use different frontends, compilers, access policies, or backends
project_relevance: Directly relevant to AI infrastructure horizontal tracking: addresses fundamental architectural mismatch in LLM serving systems, provides concrete system mechanism (runtime access plan IR), demonstrates end-to-end efficiency gains (1.08x-1.19x speedup) with quality preservation. Should be categorized under 'serving_runtime_compiler' direction. Represents paradigm shift from token-aware to knowledge-aware runtime consumption

_provenance.source_title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
